maria: heads up — trying to onboard hf:/openchat/openchat-7b-v2 via convert-bot and hitting a weird combo of safetensors shard/index missing + special_tokens_map getting clobbered. converter v0.9.2
ken: ugh, can you paste the error/logs? :eyes:
maria: here are the relevant tails from the job log:

maria: ```
convert-bot ERROR job=j-2345 loading shard 00001.safetensors
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/convert/main.py", line 214, in run
    weights = load_safetensors(shard_path)
  File "/app/convert/io.py", line 98, in load_safetensors
    raise ValueError("index not found")
ValueError: index not found
```

maria: also after an apparent successful load the tokenizer ends up with `special_tokens_map = {}` and the chat template defaults to system-only, which breaks role-tagging in our evals.
ken: couple questions: did the repo have a `safetensors.index` file? sometimes hub storage splits shards and the index is separate. did you pin a hub revision when you started the job?
maria: I didn't pin; I just gave the repo path. hub responses were flakey earlier (200 then transient 404s). convert-bot logs show a couple of auth retries:

maria: ```
WARNING: hub_download 403 after retry 2 for file shards/00001.safetensors
INFO: retrying with anonymous fallback
INFO: downloaded 00001.safetensors (but no index)
```

alex: classic. If the index isn't present at the same rev we end up streaming partial shards and the converter's shard-ordering logic collapses — which can reorder tensors and make weight key renames look mismatched.
alex: quick workaround: clone the repo at the exact commit and run conversion locally to ensure all artifacts present:

alex: ```bash
git lfs install
git clone https://huggingface.co/openchat/openchat-7b-v2
git -C openchat-7b-v2 rev-parse HEAD  # get sha
# then run:
redwood-convert --input openchat-7b-v2 --pin-rev <sha> --preserve-special-tokens --safetensors-index shards/safetensors.index
```

sasha: fwiw we saw a similar issue where weight keys between HF and our expected names differ (e.g., `q_proj.weight` vs `attn.q.weight`). converter currently attempts a best-effort rename but if shard order is off it applies renames to wrong tensors.
ken: is this why some quantized bring-ups had quality regressions? tokens shifting due to mismatched embeddings?
maria: yes — one run had `pad_token_id` change from 1 to 0 after conversion which shifted positional offsets in downstream evals. small token id mismatch can make perplexity jump.

alex: actionable items I think:
1) require `--pin-rev` as a recommended flag in the hosted UI when converting from hub; log a clear hint when index missing.
2) converter: if `safetensors.index` missing, fail fast with suggestion to pin rev or provide index path, do not fallback to anonymous partial download.
3) preserve tokenizer special tokens from tokenizer.json before applying config.json fallthrough (we should not overwrite special_tokens_map with empty dict).
4) improve key-rename heuristics and add a deterministic verification step: after mapping, check embedding shapes against tokenizer.vocab_size and warn if mismatch.

devx-bot: convert-bot j-2345 status -> FAILED (exit 1) | reason: missing safetensors.index | opened issue #1123

sasha: +1 on the verification step. We should also add a small unit test: create a fake shard ordering and assert a mapping file is applied to the correct tensor names.
ken: for immediate unblocking: maria, can you re-run the job with `--pin-rev <sha>` and attach the index file if available? also try `--preserve-special-tokens` flag I added to our local fork — it prevents the tokenizer clobber.
maria: doing that now. if that works we'll run a quick quantization smoke to check perplexity vs baseline.

maria: update — pinned rev + uploaded index -> converter finished, tokenizer preserved, embeddings align. quick eval shows token-level shift gone. sending results to bench channel after more runs. :thumbsup:

alex: i'll open a small PR to convert-bot:
- change default fallback to fail with explicit message
- add `--preserve-special-tokens` behavior by default for HF imports
- add check: if embedding matrix rows != tokenizer.vocab_size -> fail with error guiding to key-rename mapping

sasha: can you add an integration test that mocks hub auth flakiness? we keep hitting weird 403 -> anon fallback sequences.
alex: yeah, will add a flaky-hub fixture and a CI job.
ken: nice teamwork. once PR merges we'll roll to dedicated and run a couple more model bring-ups to catch regressions early.

maria: thanks all — major blocker cleared for this model. will post final perf/quality numbers tomorrow.
